items.stem: Which four parts form the Value Playbook's business case architecture?

options.text: Pipeline, forecast, invoice and renewal.
Agent count, connector count, slide count and meeting count.
Logo, product tour, discount and signature.
Problem Statement, Justification, ROI and Plan.

items.stem: When does salary-equivalent time become hard-dollar savings?

options.text: Only when a defensible actual cost/business action supports that classification.
As soon as an AI model estimates minutes.
Whenever any user says the product feels faster.
Whenever a vendor benchmark is published.

items.stem: What can survey-only presale evidence safely support?

options.text: A guaranteed CFO-grade realized saving.
A measured baseline for every user without sampling caveats.
A directional self-reported hypothesis with explicit limitations.
A causal proof of revenue increase.

items.stem: What does the recapture rate describe?

options.text: The percentage of users who can log in.
The tax rate on software purchases.
The share of saved capacity converted into useful business output.
The number of connectors in the architecture.

items.stem: For annual benefit B and annual all-in cost C greater than zero, which net ROI formula is correct?

options.text: B × C.
B + C.
C / B without any interpretation.

items.stem: A metric has no historical timing data. What belongs in its baseline field?

options.text: The desired target relabeled as baseline.
Not yet measured, with an owner and collection plan.
A generated exact number with no evidence.
A peer company's result labeled customer actual.

items.stem: Why must the author check the meaning of the time-saved input before applying efficiency?

options.text: Applying efficiency to an already measured saving may double-discount the same effect.
A larger number is always more accurate.
Efficiency is always a legal tax deduction.
Minutes never need conversion to hours.

items.stem: The downside scenario is negative. What should the learner do?

options.text: Increase recapture until all scenarios look positive.
Keep it visible, explain the drivers and use it to refine the decision and validation plan.
Rename negative return as guaranteed savings.
Delete it before the executive meeting.
